title: Dark surface with one luminous accent
summary: Build a dark interface from a near-black surface and one accent that still reads in a single color, so light and dark states stay recognizable without a second palette.
when_to_use: The user wants a developer-facing or technical page that stays comfortable in a dark theme.
avoid_when: The primary audience needs a light, high-familiarity consumer layout, or body text would sit on a glowing gradient.

anatomy.purpose: Near-black background and a slightly lifted panel, not a pure black void.
One luminous color for the active state, link, and focus ring.
Light and dark treatments of the same silhouette, both legible before any animation.

tokens.name: surface.raised
tokens.purpose: Panel one step above the page.

tokens.name: accent.primary
tokens.purpose: Single highlight used for focus, links, and the active control.

states.name: dark
states.behavior: Light text on the dark surface; accent marks the current item.

states.name: light
states.behavior: Same silhouette with inverted ink, still one accent.

responsive: Keep the accent on the control itself at narrow widths; do not move meaning into a glow that gets cropped.
accessibility: Body text uses a solid surface, not the accent glow.
The control silhouette must stay understandable in one color, including when the accent is absent.
implementation_steps: Set a near-black surface and one raised panel tone.
Assign a single accent to focus, links, and the selected state.
Define the light counterpart by inverting ink, not by inventing a second accent.
Implement the theme in the user stack. Do not copy toggle artwork or a component registry.

source_refs.license_scope: MIT design note on light and dark silhouettes that read in one color
